tEn: Designing Inflight: A Designer's Raw 0-to-1 Startup Journey
tZh: 设计 Inflight：设计师从 0 到 1 的创业幕后
sEn: Kyle Barber shares the raw behind-the-scenes story of designing Inflight, from a hacked-together side project to a startup built by designers.
sZh: Kyle Barber 讲述设计 Inflight 的真实幕后：从临时拼凑的副业项目，到由设计师亲手打造的创业公司。

consensus.en: Design thinking applies to everything: product, company culture, fundraising, and brand.
consensus.zh: 设计思维适用于一切：产品、公司文化、融资和品牌。

consensus.en: AI lets designers own code and data, becoming full product builders.
consensus.zh: AI 让设计师能够掌控代码和数据，成为完整的产品构建者。

consensus.en: Trust between founders is the most underrated ingredient for startup success.
consensus.zh: 创始人之间的信任是创业成功最被低估的要素。

consensus.en: Timing matters more than team, market size, or product for startups.
consensus.zh: 对于创业公司，时机比团队、市场规模或产品更重要。

consensus.en: Narrowing focus to a specific workflow unlocks simplicity and clarity.
consensus.zh: 将焦点缩小到特定工作流可以带来简洁和清晰。

consensus.en: Designers must be willing to delete their darlings as the market shifts.
consensus.zh: 设计师必须愿意随着市场变化而放弃自己的心血。

contrarian.en: Building too far into the future is a trap; being early is as bad as being wrong.
contrarian.zh: 过度构建未来是一个陷阱；过早和错误一样糟糕。

contrarian.en: Designers should not stay in Figma; code prototypes are the new design tool.
contrarian.zh: 设计师不应停留在 Figma；代码原型是新的设计工具。

contrarian.en: Serving every customer request leads to feature bloat and failure; hyper-narrow is better.
contrarian.zh: 满足每个客户请求会导致功能膨胀和失败；超窄聚焦更好。

contrarian.en: The best designers are not defined by big company logos but by their systems thinking.
contrarian.zh: 最好的设计师不是由大公司标志定义的，而是由他们的系统思维定义的。

contrarian.en: AI enables designers to build insight pipelines and act autonomously without pitching.
contrarian.zh: AI 使设计师能够构建洞察管道并自主行动，无需推销。

contrarian.en: Founders should treat company creation as a design problem, not follow a playbook.
contrarian.zh: 创始人应将公司创建视为设计问题，而不是遵循剧本。

turns.en: If you're creating a startup, you can make it as a designer. You don't have to follow a playbook of how someone else decided they wanted to create a company.
turns.zh: 如果你要创建一家初创公司，你可以以设计师的身份来做。你不必遵循别人决定创建公司时的剧本。

turns.en: Welcome to Dive Club. My name is Rid and this is where designers never stop learning. This week's episode is a special one for me because we get to hear from my co-founder Kyle Barber and we're going to do a deep dive into what it's like as designers going 0 to 1 on a new startup like Inflight in the middle of the insanity that is today's landscape.
turns.zh: 欢迎来到 Dive Club。我是 Rid，这里是设计师永不停歇的学习之地。本周的节目对我来说很特别，因为我们将听到我的联合创始人 Kyle Barber 的分享，我们将深入探讨设计师如何在当今疯狂的大环境中，从 0 到 1 打造一家像 Inflight 这样的新初创公司。

turns.en: I mean, I feel like I've grown as much as a designer in the last 18 months than any point in my career. So, we're going to do our best to capture that journey for you today. So without further ado, here's how it all started.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得在过去 18 个月里，我作为设计师的成长比职业生涯中任何阶段都多。所以，今天我们会尽力为大家捕捉这段旅程。那么事不宜迟，以下就是一切的开端。

turns.en: I think for most of my career, the products that I've created have just been off of a direct need essentially, like some use case that I knew. And at the time I was working with Naval Ravikant and Brian Norgard on a product called Airchat. And I was the only designer on the team. And getting feedback was interesting to say the least, like both are extremely accomplished founders and super busy, have families, and their communication style was largely through text message or Signal. And as the only designer on the team, I was just having a lot of trouble getting feedback on my work and organizing it and knowing what to do with all of that.
turns.zh: 我想在我职业生涯的大部分时间里，我创造的产品基本上都是出于直接的需求，比如我知道的某个用例。当时我和 Naval Ravikant 和 Brian Norgard 一起做一个叫 Airchat 的产品。我是团队里唯一的设计师。获得反馈这件事怎么说呢，很有趣——两人都是非常有成就的创始人，超级忙，有家庭，他们的沟通方式主要是通过短信或 Signal。作为团队里唯一的设计师，我在获取工作反馈、整理反馈以及知道如何处理所有这些方面遇到了很多困难。

turns.en: So I started hacking together a little side project in that moment and was just like what can I do to both present my work better to those two because I always wanted my work to resonate with them and also how to collect their feedback so I wasn't scrolling through months of iMessage to try to find the context of why we did or didn't do a specific decision. So just started prototyping something for my own use case and then at a certain point I was like well this is kind of helpful maybe I should share this with other people and post a little tweet about it and a lot of other designers agreed that it was something worth pursuing.
turns.zh: 于是我当时就开始拼凑一个小副业项目，想着我能做什么来更好地向那两位展示我的作品——因为我一直希望我的作品能引起他们的共鸣——同时也能收集他们的反馈，这样我就不用翻几个月的 iMessage 来找我们为什么做出或没做出某个决定的上下文了。所以就开始为我自己的用例做原型，然后到了某个时刻，我想这还挺有用的，也许我应该分享给其他人，就发了一条推文，很多其他设计师也同意这值得追求。

turns.en: So real quick message and then we can jump back into it. There's only one app on my computer that I use literally hundreds of times per day and it's Raycast. And now that they have dictation built right into Raycast 2.0 my usage has gone to a whole other level. I literally cancelled my Super Whisper subscription because it's that good. The design is as elegant as you'd expect from the Raycast team, but there are some seriously powerful features that really take it to the next level. And one of my favorites is styles. It allows you to set up custom instructions for specific apps and websites. So, I can get clean prompts when I'm building in code or even automatically structure my output as markdown when I'm dictating the dive newsletter. It's just another reason why Raycast is the very first thing I recommend installing on a computer. So, if you're somehow not using it already, head to dive.club/raycast to sign up.
turns.zh: 快速说个消息，然后我们继续。我电脑上只有一个应用我每天 literally 用几百次，那就是 Raycast。现在他们把听写功能直接内置到 Raycast 2.0 里，我的使用量又上了一个新台阶。我 literally 取消了 Super Whisper 的订阅，因为它就是那么好。设计一如既往地优雅，符合你对 Raycast 团队的期待，但还有一些非常强大的功能真正把它提升到了新水平。我最喜欢的功能之一是样式。它允许你为特定应用和网站设置自定义指令。所以我在写代码时可以得到干净的提示，甚至在口述 Dive 新闻稿时自动将输出结构化为 Markdown。这只是我推荐在电脑上安装的第一个东西是 Raycast 的又一个原因。所以，如果你还没在用，请前往 dive.club/raycast 注册。

turns.en: I think it's safe to say that this is your last chance to be early on Paper. And it feels like everybody is talking about it on Twitter. I mean, guests are constantly bringing it up on this show. They just raised a massive Series A and Paper's pretty quickly become the design tool of choice for people shipping with agents. It really feels like it was built specifically for this new way of working and that's a big reason why I use it every single day. So, if you're still sleeping, head to dive.club/paper and I think you're really quickly going to realize why so many designers are making the switch. Now, on to the episode.
turns.zh: 可以说这是你成为 Paper 早期用户的最后机会。感觉 Twitter 上人人都在谈论它。我的意思是，嘉宾们不断在节目中提起它。他们刚刚完成了大规模 A 轮融资，Paper 很快成为用智能体交付产品的人的首选设计工具。它真的感觉是专门为这种新的工作方式而构建的，这也是我每天使用它的一个重要原因。所以，如果你还在观望，请前往 dive.club/paper，我想你很快就会明白为什么这么多设计师在转向它。现在，回到节目。

turns.en: I remember reconnecting with you during this season for the first time in like at least a few years. You were saying you were working on a thing. You gave me a little teaser. It was cool and I was kind of willing you to do it, but then Airchat had the viral moment. I will still die on the hill that the two weeks where Airchat first launched was the most fun that I've ever had on social media which kind of delayed things. It was kind of interesting to see when you were going to make the jump because I think it probably took a little bit longer than you thought.
turns.zh: 我记得在这个季节第一次和你重新联系，至少有好几年没见了。你说你在做一个东西，给了我一点预告。很酷，我有点在鼓励你去做，但后来 Airchat 有了病毒式传播的时刻。我仍然坚持认为 Airchat 刚发布的那两周是我在社交媒体上玩得最开心的时光，这有点推迟了事情。看到你什么时候会跳出来挺有意思的，因为我觉得这可能比你想象的要花更长一点时间。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: I think my whole career I've been having a side project no matter what. So, this was always kind of like this is a pretty good side project, but for the first time, it wasn't an awful idea. I think I was making towels and pens and random sports apps and a bunch of things for myself that never actually connected. And this was the one I was like, 'Okay, there's enough behind this. Maybe it's worth going for.'
turns.zh: 我想我整个职业生涯无论怎样都有一个副业项目。所以这一直就像是一个相当不错的副业项目，但这是第一次，它不是一个糟糕的想法。我想我做过毛巾、笔、随机的体育应用以及一堆为自己做的东西，但从未真正连接起来。而这个是让我觉得‘好吧，这背后有足够的东西。也许值得一试。’

turns.en: At what point, like, take us to that moment where you realized that it was worth going for. What happened?
turns.zh: 在哪个时刻，带我们回到你意识到它值得追求的那一刻。发生了什么？

turns.en: I think there were a lot of different shades of that because there was an initial concept which was just like this marketplace, right? That is it's not really a VC fundable company and it was more just like who can I get on board to just share critique like you upload something and maybe pay $20 kind of like intro.co if you ever use that and you can just have a designer just come in quickly and review your work on a high level and that would have been cool like I actually think there's still probably business out there if someone wanted to do that but the economics you know it's a hard one to pull off so I thought it could be something on the side while I was doing other work and you know maybe just have this little network or marketplace business going and I actually don't fully remember when it transitioned to be like okay that idea probably isn't going to be like a big one but there's another one it honestly might have been talking with you where we're just like could we build this for teams is there something else that's not just pure
turns.zh: 我觉得有很多不同的层次，因为最初的概念就像这个市场，对吧？那并不是一个真正可获风投投资的公司，更像是：我能拉谁进来分享批评，比如你上传一些东西，也许付 20 美元，有点像 intro.co 如果你用过的话，你可以让一个设计师快速进来，高层次地审查你的作品，那本来会很酷——我实际上认为如果有人想做，可能仍然有生意可做，但经济模型你知道，很难实现。所以我认为它可以是我做其他工作时的一个副业，也许只是拥有这个小网络或市场业务。我实际上不完全记得什么时候转变成了‘好吧，那个想法可能不会成为大生意，但还有另一个’。老实说，可能是在和你交谈时，我们就在想我们能不能为团队构建这个，有没有其他不只是纯粹……

transcript.sec: The Pivot to a Design Tool

turns.en: I remember the moment we were working at this point for context for people listening like when I joined Inflight was a marketplace for design feedback that was what I was excited about we started working on it we had this incredible roster of a bunch of people that would review your work and a lot of them had been like guests on the show that was presenting its own challenges but then there was one day where we had to make a tool in order for people to submit their work and then the reviewers to come in and I remember Ver our other co-founder and he made this product where like the original video cursor and you could fly around on the canvas but it wasn't even a video it was actually just cursor tracking and I remember we were testing that and I had this moment where I was like oh my gosh I would use this instead of Loom like I've used Loom in every past roll and it just felt like complete magic where at least for me that was the moment it was like oh shoot are we making design tool.
turns.zh: 我记得那一刻，我们当时在工作——为听众提供背景，当我加入 Inflight 时，它是一个设计反馈市场，那是我兴奋的地方。我们开始做它，我们有一群不可思议的人来审查你的作品，其中很多人上过节目，这带来了自己的挑战。但后来有一天，我们不得不做一个工具，让人们提交作品，然后让审查者进来。我记得我们的另一位联合创始人 Ver，他做了这个产品，就像最初的视频光标，你可以在画布上飞来飞去，但它甚至不是视频，实际上只是光标跟踪。我记得我们在测试它，我有那么一刻，我想‘天哪，我会用这个而不是 Loom’。我在过去的每个职位都用 Loom，它感觉完全是魔法。至少对我来说，那一刻就像是‘哦，糟糕，我们是在做设计工具吗？’

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And I remember, I mean, it was still Figma land, so there were a lot of interesting technical challenges of how to pull all this off. Like we were trying to embed the Figma files inside of some iframe and had a bunch of—we had a Figma plugin as well that would take all your screens...
turns.zh: 我记得，我的意思是，当时还是 Figma 的天下，所以有很多有趣的技术挑战需要克服。比如我们试图把 Figma 文件嵌入到某个 iframe 里，还有一堆——我们也有一个 Figma 插件，可以把你所有的屏幕……

turns.en: The whole product... makes you think jeez there was a lot of iterations there.
turns.zh: 整个产品……让人不禁想，天哪，那里有很多次迭代。

turns.en: And even just stepping back for a second, like I think one of my goals for this conversation is to just capture the winding journey because we set out to build a product—I mean originally you set out to build a product that solves your—I joined because I really resonated with this problem space of getting feedback. It's something that I've cared a lot about. I've only worked remotely for a very long time. You know, we wanted to build a thing for ourselves and yet the very nature of our day-to-day and our job changed so extremely over the—like we chose to build a tooling company in the most insane 18 months in the history of tech tools. And thinking through product strategy and positioning associated with that has been really challenging and my hope is that it actually can be enlightening for a lot of people. And so maybe even just continuing on with the journey—like we have a tool, what we think we have a tool—what do you even remember from that season of even figuring out like is there something here, what should we be building, that kind of a thing?
turns.zh: 甚至退一步说，我觉得这次对话的目标之一就是记录这段曲折的旅程，因为我们一开始是要打造一个产品——我的意思是，最初你是要打造一个解决你自己问题的产品——我加入是因为我真的很共鸣于获取反馈这个领域。这是我一直很关心的事情。我长期只做远程工作。你知道，我们想为自己打造一个东西，但我们日常工作和工作的本质在这段——我们选择在科技工具史上最疯狂的 18 个月里创办一家工具公司。思考与之相关的产品策略和定位真的很有挑战性，我希望这能对很多人有启发。所以也许就继续这段旅程——比如我们有一个工具，我们认为我们有一个工具——你甚至还记得那个阶段 figuring out 这里有没有东西、我们应该打造什么之类的事情吗？

turns.en: Well, it's probably just a testament for launching a lot and getting it in user hands, which is something I think we've done well the whole time.
turns.zh: 嗯，这 probably 只是对大量发布并让用户使用的证明，我认为这是我们一直做得好的地方。

turns.en: And it actually just made me think of the very first concept, which was actually an internal tool for me that I then posted about and had so many people share their work. Like it wasn't meant to be a marketplace, but I had like hundreds of people uploading designs, Figma files. Like the initial prototype was just paste your Figma link and then I'll record a voiceover on top of it. And I was doing that like I did like a hundred times and I was like wait a minute, like should I be like—someone sent me $20 out of nowhere, like they're asking, they're like can I just pay you for the review? Like it was super helpful. And then I got that moment I was like wait a minute, like should we like connect other people with other—like if there's money being transferred here that's a good sign. But it's funny, like the loop of it, cuz it was just a tool for teams and then marketplace and then we tested the marketplace with more people and they're like you would have to pay—we had some huge designers on there that were maybe $300 an hour, right? Like that's not it, like to review—like that's the amount and it just wasn't working. But we launched, right? We like saw it, we had people give us feedback, we switch. Like I think we've done that a 100 times. And so in one way that's really good to get to like a source of truth of what's a good product. On another way it's really hard to—two designers and constantly in this perfectionist state like editing and saying it's not good enough over and over again.
turns.zh: 这实际上让我想到了最初的概念，那其实是我的一个内部工具，然后我发布了它，很多人分享了他们的作品。它本来不是要做一个市场，但有数百人上传设计、Figma 文件。最初的原型就是粘贴你的 Figma 链接，然后我在上面录一段语音。我做了大概一百次，然后我想等等，我是不是应该——有人突然给我转了 20 美元，他们问，能不能就付钱请你评审？这超级有帮助。然后我有了那个时刻，我想等等，我们是不是应该把其他人和其他人连接起来——如果这里有金钱转移，那是个好迹象。但有趣的是它的循环，因为它最初只是给团队的工具，然后是市场，然后我们用更多人测试市场，他们说你需要付费——我们那里有一些大牌设计师，可能每小时 300 美元，对吧？那不行，评审——那个金额，就是行不通。但我们发布了，对吧？我们看到了，我们得到了反馈，我们切换。我想我们做了 100 次。所以一方面，这对于找到什么是好产品的真相来源非常有好处。另一方面，真的很难——两个设计师不断处于这种完美主义状态，编辑并说不够好，一遍又一遍。

turns.en: Yeah, there's a slippery slope there for sure. Like this was the very first time that I've worked early stage with another designer in my entire career. I've only done the zero to one thing and I've only been the only designer. I think there was a lot of, you know, growing pains figuring out not only that but like we worked very very differently as designers too.
turns.zh: 是的，那里肯定有一个滑坡。比如这是我职业生涯中第一次在早期阶段与另一位设计师合作。我只做过从零到一的事情，而且我一直是唯一的设计师。我觉得有很多，你知道，成长的痛苦，不仅要弄清楚这一点，还有我们作为设计师的工作方式也非常非常不同。

turns.en: It's kind of fascinating how we're both technically—like I was an employed designer like at Meta, you know, we both had full product designer jobs but I think we have like 5% overlap in the Venn diagram of what it means to be a designer. I'm coming from having taught hundreds of enterprise teams how to use Figma at a high level, like auto layout everything, frames over groups, everything's super organized, components, a little bit of a neat freak in Figma. And then I would try to iterate on your files and you're like—
turns.zh: 这有点迷人，我们俩在技术上——比如我在 Meta 做过受雇设计师，你知道，我们都有全职产品设计师的工作，但我认为在设计师意味着什么的维恩图上，我们只有 5% 的重叠。我来自教过数百个企业团队如何高水平使用 Figma，比如所有东西都用自动布局，用框架而不是组，一切超级有条理，组件，在 Figma 里有点洁癖。然后我试着在你的文件上迭代，你就说——

turns.en: Rectangles, groups, never do—you probably don't even—to the day, you still to this day you probably don't know the keyboard shortcut for auto layout, like—
turns.zh: 矩形、组，从来不做——你可能甚至——直到今天，你到今天可能还不知道自动布局的键盘快捷键，就像——

turns.en: I've never—I've used auto layout like one time in my life. Like I just—I don't know. I came from—I started in Photoshop, right, and everything was like folders, and then Sketch came along, everything was folders. Like I don't know, this is just my mental model. I've always just wanted to like make the product right. Like I just wanted to get it in people's hands and the craft part of me—like it was always just fulfilling the need. Like I didn't want to launch something that didn't look great, so I taught myself that, but I definitely index further on the product side where I think you're much more like craft, like design UI, interaction.
turns.zh: 我从来没有——我这辈子大概只用过一次自动布局。就像我只是——我不知道。我来自——我从 Photoshop 开始，对吧，一切都是文件夹，然后 Sketch 出现了，一切都是文件夹。就像我不知道，这只是我的心智模型。我一直只是想做出正确的产品。就像我只是想把它交到人们手中，而我工艺的那部分——就像它总是只是满足需求。就像我不想发布一个看起来不好的东西，所以我自学了那个，但我肯定更偏向产品侧，而我认为你更偏向工艺，比如设计 UI、交互。

turns.en: It took us a little bit to kind of have that flipping though, cuz you were the original person—like I remember when you first like quote unquote onboarded me, cuz I joined like months after you and Ver had started working on the first version of the product and you showed me like a real product. Like you had made a real product. You had designed all of it. It looked good. I remember being almost caught off guard by how far you were and then getting it. I remember where I was. Dude, I remember where I was. I was at my friend's pool and you texted me something along the lines of like, 'Hey man, I think we should switch. Like I think you should do more of the design.' Like designers are such a special class and I feel like we've been devalued a little bit where it's like, well, we could just do everything in code. I want to still celebrate the thinking of that and I think Inflight's like the vehicle for that. You know what I mean?
turns.zh: 这是个难题。我觉得当我们缩小范围后，事情开始变得清晰一些。嗯，你知道，我们现在要推向市场的产品，我看着它就想，这是一个美丽、深思熟虑、有价值的产品，我们已经和数百名设计师和团队测试过，反馈很好。人们确实从中获得了价值。这一直是目标，对吧？就是做出有价值的东西。现在它已经实现了，你就得换个帽子，对吧？你会想，好吧，我们如何发展业务？如何创造销售势头？如何锁定营销？你知道，我们最近开始和 Tommy 合作，对吧？很棒的联合创始人。他非常擅长这些。我很兴奋能真正建立一家企业，而不仅仅是概念化产品和用例。嗯，我们还有一些相当大的赌注即将到来。我们处于独特的位置，可以做一些非常酷的事情。我很兴奋能翻过一直在代码和 Figma 中协作的这一页，然后说，酷，让我们为那些已经发现价值的人创造更多价值。以至于他们愿意告诉朋友他们喜欢使用 Inflight。我们已经看到了——它在增长。有些团队它简直就是公司的核心。总的来说，这让我非常高兴，我们终于能够以一款对人们有效的工具走到另一端。所以此时我想，好吧，下一步是什么？现在我们必须再次成为创始人，摆脱这种‘哦，一直只是代码模式’的状态。也许那就是社区。我期待看到你和 Tommy 也许举办一些晚宴和活动，真正建立品牌。我们这里有一个很棒的创始团队，我想我们已经——我们有一个 Discord 社区正在发展。我们一直想为设计师做出伟大的东西，我们认为这是一个很好的方式来赋能他们并围绕此创建社区。也许你可以多谈谈你是否看到任何机会。但我很想回到早期 Dribbble 的日子，他们分发篮球和 T 恤，在世界各地举办聚会和 Figma 聚会。设计师是一个如此特殊的群体，我觉得我们被贬低了一点，就好像，好吧，我们可以用代码做一切。我想仍然庆祝这种思考，我认为 Inflight 是其中的载体。你明白我的意思吗？

turns.en: I think the potential for that is pretty exciting. I make content because I like sharing and I like, you know, sometimes that even takes the form of teaching. And by teaching, it's literally just like, hey, I learned this today. Like, and just being quick to share, right? I'm really excited to get back into that, too. Like, I think it's actually been really hard while navigating all of the different pivots and changes to figure out what that looks like. And there's part of me that's always my natural disposition. And so, being able to settle back like, dude, I just changed our icon library the other day. I don't even know if you realized, but I switched it to Central. I know you didn't. I know you didn't. Everything—every single icon in the entire product is different. So, I switched it to Central because I put a tweet out and I was like, 'What are the cool kids using for icon libraries?' I had no idea that—uh—the iconists had this library, which I'm embarrassed by, but I built really cool tools to transition the icon library and I was able to do it all in like an hour from these three jigs that I built. And then I built my own web app to be able to switch the icons. Anyway, you can tell I'm just getting nerdy about this. This is not the rabbit hole I want to go down. The point is just getting back to sharing what you're learning and building community around that is always where my heart is at. So I'm excited about that. I'm also excited to be in a position to think about the forefront of where all these products are going and what that means for us too. And the big thing on my mind right now is we really even in the last week have embraced the MCP is everything.
turns.zh: 我觉得这方面的潜力非常令人兴奋。我制作内容是因为我喜欢分享，而且你知道，有时这甚至采取教学的形式。而教学，实际上就是，嘿，我今天学到了这个。然后快速分享，对吧？我也真的很兴奋能回到那种状态。我觉得在应对所有不同的转向和变化时，要弄清楚那是什么样子真的很难。而我的一部分始终是我的天性。所以，能够安定下来，就像，老兄，我前几天刚换了我们的图标库。我甚至不知道你有没有注意到，但我把它换成了 Central。我知道你没有。我知道你没有。整个产品中的每一个图标都不同了。所以，我把它换成了 Central，因为我发了一条推文，我说，‘酷孩子们用什么图标库？’我完全不知道——呃——iconists 有这个库，这让我很尴尬，但我构建了非常酷的工具来转换图标库，我能够在大约一个小时内用我构建的三个 jig 完成所有工作。然后我构建了自己的网络应用来切换图标。总之，你可以看出我只是在这方面变得很书呆子。这不是我想深入探讨的兔子洞。重点只是回到分享你正在学习的东西，并围绕此建立社区，这一直是我心之所向。所以我对此很兴奋。我也很兴奋能处于一个思考所有这些产品的前沿以及这对我们意味着什么的位置。现在我脑海中最重要的事情是，我们真的甚至在上周就接受了 MCP 就是一切。

turns.en: I expect every tool that I use to work inside of Conductor, which really forces you to—it's a reckoning as a designer who is working on a product. I've spent a lot of time working on different forms of dashboards, and like, dude, I don't really use the dashboards that much anymore, which is weird, right? Like, that's really hard.
turns.zh: 我希望我用的每个工具都能在 Conductor 里跑通，这对做产品的设计师来说真的是一种清算。我花了很多时间做各种形式的仪表盘，说实话，我现在其实不太用仪表盘了，这很奇怪，对吧？这真的很难。

turns.en: And we've seen so many different internal tools built by these teams, and actually everything about Inflight now just fits into whatever your internal system already is, versus asking you to use our system instead.
turns.zh: 我们见过这些团队搭的各种内部工具，而现在 Inflight 的一切其实都能融进你已有的内部系统里，而不是要求你来用我们的系统。

turns.en: Where does that go, and what does that mean for growth and positioning and storytelling? And we have a, you know, ChatGPT app or plugin and review, and like, what does that mean? What is it?
turns.zh: 那这会走向哪里？这对增长、定位和叙事意味着什么？我们还有个 ChatGPT 应用或插件，还有 review，那意味着什么？那到底是什么？

turns.en: I'm excited to be at the forefront of what it looks like to atomize UI and bake little parts of a product experience into a chat and have everything be agent driven. And, you know, probably having guests on the podcast to learn what they're doing and figure out what that means for Inflight and kind of bring people along for the journey—like, that's going to be such an exciting and new chapter for us. And it's one of, you know, five different answers that I could have given there.
turns.zh: 我很兴奋能站在最前沿，去探索把 UI 原子化、把产品体验的一小部分嵌进聊天里、让一切都由智能体驱动会是什么样子。而且大概还会请嘉宾上播客，了解他们在做什么，弄清那对 Inflight 意味着什么，带着大家一起走这段路——那对我们来说会是非常激动人心的新篇章。这也只是我本可以给出的五个不同答案之一。

turns.en: So it's a fun time to be a designer. It's a fun time to work with friends. It's a fun time to go zero to one on new ideas. And I'm pretty jazzed about everything as a result.
turns.zh: 所以现在做设计师很有意思。和朋友一起做事很有意思。把新想法从零做到一很有意思。因此我对这一切都挺兴奋的。

turns.en: Fun time to have something that people—it's always the goal of the designer, right? Like, make something useful.
turns.zh: 能做出让人——这始终是设计师的目标，对吧？就是做出有用的东西。

turns.en: I think a hope that I have from this conversation is that more people realize that they don't have to have the answers or even the perfect idea. You can kind of just start doing something and arrive there just because you can build really quickly. You're not as reliant on other people in the way that you were historically.
turns.zh: 我对这次对话的一个期望，是让更多人意识到，他们不必先有答案，甚至不必有完美的点子。你完全可以先动手做点什么，然后自然走到那里，因为你现在能很快地把东西做出来。你不再像过去那样依赖别人。

turns.en: And also, like, as designers, we're just problem solvers. We just figure it out, you know? Like, you could just pick a path and explore and find problems and solve problems and then iterate. And I hope that more people do that. Like, I hope that even just one person listens to this and they're like, you know what, I'm going to get off the fence and take my first step toward creating a thing that I own and get to run with.
turns.zh: 而且，作为设计师，我们就是解决问题的人。我们就是把它搞明白，你懂的。你完全可以选一条路，去探索，发现问题、解决问题，然后迭代。我希望更多人这么做。哪怕只有一个人听了这期节目，然后想：你知道吗，我要不再观望了，迈出第一步，去做一个属于我自己、由我来推进的东西。

turns.en: Couldn't have said it better. Hey, if you enjoyed this episode, don't forget that every Thursday I go live with Tommy Goyoko for Dive Radio, where we deep dive into trending topics and hear from a ton of incredible designers in the industry. So, if you want to get that on your calendar, just go to dive.comclub/radio. And I'll see you on Thursdays at 4:00 p.m. Eastern.
turns.zh: 说得再好不过了。嘿，如果你喜欢这期节目，别忘了每周四我都会和 Tommy Goyoko 一起直播 Dive Radio，我们会深入聊热门话题，也会听到业内许多了不起的设计师分享。如果你想把它加进日历，就去 dive.comclub/radio。我们周四美东时间下午 4 点见。

tldr.en: Design thinking applies to product, culture, fundraising, and brand—not just UI.
tldr.zh: 设计思维不仅用于界面，更适用于产品、文化、融资和品牌。

tldr.en: AI lets designers own code and data, becoming full product builders.
tldr.zh: AI 让设计师能掌控代码和数据，成为完整的产品构建者。

tldr.en: Timing matters more than team, market size, or product for startups.
tldr.zh: 对初创公司而言，时机比团队、市场规模或产品更重要。
